locator.text: Equation (A.38), p. 138, in the proof of Lemma A.6

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has a weaker form of it. Both equalities are stated. The first is heated_exterior (E_heat = (power amplitude)·X^{-A}·H(2(1-η²)/X)), in product rather than quotient form, with d = 1-η² as fixed on p. 137; heatFactor_eq_profile states the ratio factor itself. The undifferentiated expansion is stated more strongly than the paper writes it: small_argument_remainder gives the explicit remainder constant h(1+h)²(2+h)z², so at z = 2d/X the remainder is ≤ 4h(1+h)²(2+h)d²/X² rather than an unspecified O_h(X^{-2}), with matching leading coefficient 2h(1+h)d/X. What is weaker is the subscript j,m: the paper asserts the same expansion with an X^{-2} remainder after every fixed application of ((X∂_X)^j ∂_η^m), and no declaration was found that states a differentiated expansion at remainder order X^{-2}. The derivative-level statements found instead bound jets at order X^{-1} (ExtendedHeatDebts.editJet_bound, ParametricHeatTail.editJet_bound, HeatProfileExtension.scaledProfile_derivative_bound, HeatTailEdit.multiplier_sub_one_bound with the sharp constant 2νh(1+h)), i.e. the repository replaces the differentiated expansion by a sharp first-order jet bound. The ingredients for a differentiated version are present (first_jet_remainder for one derivative, second_jet_bound and derivative_bound_rising for all orders), so this is a gap in assembly rather than a missing estimate; I did not verify that the general (j,m) case assembles in a few lines.
